question: If a country stopped trading with the rest of the world, whose spending power would fall the most?
answer: The poorest tenth of households. Across 40 countries, closing trade would cut real income by about 63% for the poorest tenth and 28% for the richest tenth, on average. Poorer families spend more of their money on food and goods that cross borders; richer ones spend more on local services such as restaurants and care.
move: Ask what share of each budget a change touches, not who buys luxuries.
ask: Which of the everyday things I buy cheaply exist only because they cross a border?
trap: Picturing imported luxuries, so assuming the rich would lose most.
